newsitem.title: USA: USAir calls for free slots at Heathrow.
newsitem.headline: USAir calls for free slots at Heathrow.

text.p: USAir Group Inc said on Wednesday that U.S. airlines should be provided with free slots at London's Heathrow Airport and be given access to ground facilities on "reasonable terms."

USAir's statement came after British Airways said it wanted "fair market value" for 168 take-off and landing slots that regulators say the U.K. airline and AMR Corp must give up before their proposed alliance can be approved.
USAir contends that British Airways has received slots without charge at slot-controlled O'Hare Airport in Chicago and J.F.K. International Airport in New York.
In a letter to U.S. Transportation Secretary Frederico Pena released by USAir, the airline said conditions placed on the proposed alliance "fall far short of what is required" to ensure competition.
In order to "protect consumers," U.S. carriers must be able to provide competitive service from their principal hubs, USAir said.
"This will require 30 daily additional round-trips, at a minimum," USAir said.
USAir also said British Airways must end its relationship with USAir by giving up its board seats and its equity investment. British Airways owns 24.6 percent of USAir.
